title: What level of differential check does a behaviour-preserving change need?
body:
`CLAUDE.md` says a behaviour-preserving change is checked with the differential sweep. The sweep is `tmp-claude/2026-11-02-refactor-survey/alphabet/sweep.sh`. It makes 7,376 CLI runs over every fixture, mode and flag, and we diff the outputs against the same runs from a before binary built in a worktree of the old commit. The rule has one level. Moving a `collect` in `sufr/src/lib.rs` gets the same check as changing `merge_sort`.

For sufr-e1ec81 Jack skipped the sweep in conversation. `cargo test` and a spot check of `count`, `locate` and `extract` on one fixture stood in for it. No rule says when that is enough.

## Proposal

Add a heuristic to the rule that picks the check from the kind of change. Candidate levels, cheapest first.

| level | check | kind of change |
|---|---|---|
| tests | `cargo test` | a change that moves a call in the CLI and leaves the library's search code alone |
| spot | tests, plus one fixture through each touched subcommand against the before binary | a change in how a subcommand assembles its output |
| sweep | the full differential sweep | a change under `build/`, in the `.sufr` writer or reader, or in a search path |

## Open

- Whether three levels are right, and what test places a change in one.
- Whether the sweep script gets checked in. The rule depends on it and it is untracked.

Jack asked for this review after sufr-e1ec81 lands and before the next code change.
close_reason: Jack decided on 2026-11-03 to drop the differential sweep rather than grade it. sufr-25f57e moves what the sweep checked into sufr/tests/cli.rs and rewrites the CLAUDE.md sentence.
